title: Prayer asks for God’s kingdom to fill the earth
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Hiram, Ohio, on 30 October 1831. It may have come during a Sunday meeting at the home of John and Elsa Johnson. William E. McLellin, who preached there that day, made an early copy. He linked it to the request “Thy kingdom come” in the Lord’s Prayer. The scribe of the original is unknown.
summary: The revelation describes a mighty voice from on high calling people to “prepare ye the way of the Lord” and make his paths straight. It says the keys of the kingdom of God are committed to men on earth. From there the gospel will roll forth like the stone cut from the mountain without hands. The voice calls people to prepare the supper of the Lamb and make ready for the Bridegroom. It tells them to pray and make known the Lord’s works. They are to call on the Lord so his kingdom may go forth. It says the Son of Man will come down to meet the kingdom of God set up on earth. The section ends as a prayer that the kingdom of God go forth so the kingdom of heaven may come.

contextNote.title: Keys already on the earth
contextNote.text: The revelation asks how God’s kingdom will reach the whole earth. Verse 2 answers that the keys are already “committed unto man on the earth” in this day. It compares the gospel to the stone in Daniel, cut out without hands, that fills the earth. Verses 4–5 then turn the hearer to prayer for that kingdom to go forth. Verse 6 links the two kingdoms: one goes forth so that the other may come. In this passage, the keys are authority already on earth, and prayer asks God to spread it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 64–66 presents this section as a revelation on prayer. Verses 5–6 pray for two kingdoms; how could their relationship shape what you mean when you pray “thy kingdom come”?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, Ohio, 30 October 1831, a revelation on prayer. JSP historical introduction suggests (not certain) a Sunday meeting at the Johnson home and notes McLellin’s copy and his link to Matthew 6:10. John Johnson and McLellin are included from the setting; neither is named in the text. The Daniel 2 stone image in the context note is a scripture cross-reference, not from JSP. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary sentence on the Son of Man now attributed to the text (historical voice). Setting confirmed against JSP.
